name: Infantry_Claude
author: Infantry AI
description: The Claude Code harness (HARNESS H7b-2/3): launches claude (by default the interactive CLI in a terminal; headless: -p stream-json, or the persistent --input-format stream-json), reads its event stream, maps tool approval to permission modes, routes its tool calls through the watched runner, lists its models, and reads its session store and plan limits. Setting harness.claude.liveIdleMinutes ( default 0 = never): minutes a resting live claude process may idle before it is stopped; each live process holds about 150-400 MB of RAM while it exists, so lower it to reclaim memory from sessions nobody wakes (the next wake resumes). Setting harness.claude.mode (default interactive): interactive runs the interactive claude in a pseudo-terminal (ConPTY on Windows) and reads its session transcript, so requests are the CLI's own (labelled cli); headless runs claude -p stream-json (the SDK path, labelled sdk-cli) and is used only when set explicitly. Interactive mode answers the CLI's folder trust question for the session's worktree, always passes --strict-mcp-config (so a project .mcp.json is not loaded and its approval dialog never shows), and a one-shot run (keep-alive 0) has no watch hook in it. Tool approval: deny runs claude with --permission-mode dontAsk; in every mode but allowAll an interactive claude answers its permission dialogs through a PermissionRequest hook (deny; ask relays the call to the owner), and a dialog no hook answered is answered No, so a turn never hangs on it. Setting harness.claude.approvalHookSeconds (default 1800): how long claude waits for that answer. The first turn an interactive claude is sent is watched: settings harness.claude.firstTurnSubmitSeconds (default 30) and harness.claude.firstTurnReplySeconds (default 300) bound how long the CLI may take to accept the pasted prompt and how long its first request may go unanswered; a miss gets one recovery (Enter or a re-paste; Esc and a short nudge), a second miss fails the turn with the screen tail, so a stuck start is never silent until the stall watchdog.

fields.label: Stop a resting live claude after (minutes, 0 = never)
Mode: interactive (default, the Claude Code CLI as a person runs it) or headless (SDK stream-json, claude -p)
Seconds claude waits for a tool approval answer (ask mode waits for the owner); past it the dialog is answered No
Seconds an interactive claude has to take its first prompt after the paste (then one retry, then the turn fails with the screen; 0 = never)
Seconds an interactive claude's first request has to answer after it took the prompt (then Esc and one nudge, then the turn fails with the screen; 0 = never)
How Claude Code signs in: api-key (an Anthropic API key) or subscription-login (your Claude subscription, signed in with `claude auth login` in a terminal). Empty = not chosen yet

credential.label: Claude Code
credential.help: Create an API key in the Anthropic Console (console.anthropic.com). Only needed when you choose API key; with a Claude subscription you log in instead.

credentials.label: Remote runners: Claude subscription token
credentials.help: Only for remote runners (a machine or container where nobody can log in): run `claude setup-token` and paste the token. In subscription mode it signs in a session that has no `claude auth login` of its own (a runner container); a runner set to subscription-login keeps its own login.
